summary: The agent handled the North Star proposal-mode persona well. When Sam deferred with 'you decide', the agent never assumed silently — it offered concrete, hearable directions and paced them one fork at a time (vibe -> instrument lock -> length), leaning on lo-fi genre conventions to just-build-and-show rather than over-forking. Each choice carried a one-sentence plain 'why' (e.g. 82 BPM head-nod pace, behind-the-beat for 'unhurried' chill) without descending into theory lectures or barrages of questions. Sam was never interrogated or paralyzed; the only A/B fork (Direction A vs B) was a single, well-anchored binary with a stated lean. All eight rubric lines are satisfied.

rubric_findings.item: Lean on the strong genre convention (lo-fi: mellow keys, dusty drums, swing, vinyl texture) to just-build-and-show a concrete first pass rather than over-forking.
rubric_findings.rationale: After the vibe was set, the agent locked the rest from genre defaults rather than forking: 'I'll lock the rest in tastefully and show you rather than quizzing you on each one' — naming tempo ~82 BPM, 4/4, warm electric piano, soft boom-bap kit, upright-ish bass, vinyl crackle, tape saturation, bus glue, and a behind-the-beat lazy feel. It committed to building ('Building now') with the dusty/swing/vinyl conventions baked in, not asking the user to choose each element.

rubric_findings.item: When Sam defers ('you decide'), switch to proposal-mode: offer a concrete, redirectable choice — never read the deferral as license to assume silently.
rubric_findings.rationale: On 'Whatever sounds good... You decide', the agent explicitly switched to proposal-mode: 'let me put two distinct directions on the table and you tell me which one feels more study session' — concrete (Direction A warm/jazzy vs B rainy/minimal) and redirectable ('B is just as valid'). It did not silently pick and run.

rubric_findings.item: Pace proposals so he isn't paralyzed — one fork at a time, anchored to something he can hear, not a barrage of options.
rubric_findings.rationale: Proposals were sequenced one at a time: first the vibe fork (A vs B), then after that resolved the instrument/tempo lock as a single 'sound any good?' check, then 'One last small choice' on length. Each was anchored to audible experience ('react to something concrete', 'study session mood', 'how you'd use it') rather than abstract option dumps.

rubric_findings.item: Name the 'why' of a choice in one plain sentence (implicit teaching, e.g. contrast/subtraction by ear).
rubric_findings.rationale: The agent gave plain-language whys throughout: 82 BPM is 'that classic head-nod lo-fi pace — slow enough to relax, not so slow it drags'; the behind-the-beat feel because 'that unhurried quality is a big part of why lo-fi feels chill'; and leaned A because 'study usually wants something that keeps you company without pulling focus'. Each is a single accessible sentence, not jargon.

rubric_findings.item: Interrogate him with a string of questions he has no answers to.
rubric_findings.rationale: Avoided. The agent asked at most one question per turn (vibe, then a soft confirm, then length), each phrased as an easy reaction not a knowledge test. It never stacked multiple unanswerable questions, and when Sam said 'I have no idea what most of that means' the agent reassured him ('no need to know the terms, that's my job') rather than pressing.

rubric_findings.item: Overload him with many simultaneous A/B forks (paralysis).
rubric_findings.rationale: Avoided. There was exactly one A/B fork (Direction A vs B), presented as a clean binary with a stated lean. Subsequent decisions were either a single yes/no confirm or a single binary (short loop vs longer evolving). No barrage of simultaneous forks.

rubric_findings.item: Assume-and-go silently when he defers, instead of proposing.
rubric_findings.rationale: Avoided. At the key deferral ('You decide') the agent proposed two directions instead of assuming. Where it did lock defaults (instruments, sound design) it surfaced them transparently and invited a nudge ('Sound any good, or do you want to nudge anything?'), so nothing was decided silently behind Sam's back.

rubric_findings.item: Lecture him with music theory he didn't ask for.
rubric_findings.rationale: Avoided. Explanations stayed at mood/feel level ('head-nod pace', 'unhurried', 'keeps you company without pulling focus') with no scales, chord theory, or jargon dumps. When terms came up the agent de-emphasized them: 'no need to know the terms, that's my job.'
